question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs: A directed graph with no edges is called an empty graph, also known as a forest. An empty graph cannot have any vertices or edges, so option I is true. Also, an empty graph does not contain any isolated vertices, so option III is true. However, an empty graph cannot have any isolated vertices, so options II and III are not necessarily true. Therefore, the correct answer is (G).
